record.original_question: Given a positive distance d and a plane figure, or more generally a body in space, determine the largest number of points that can be placed in the figure so that every pair of chosen points is at distance at least d. Also determine the smallest set of points {A1, A2, ...} in such a figure with the property that every additional point A in the figure lies within distance d of at least one Ai.

evidence.quote: Let d > o. Questions: (a) What is the maximum number of points included in a plane figure (generally: in a space body) such that the distance between any two points is greater than or equal to d? (b) What is the minimum number of points {A1, A2,...} included in a plane figure ... such that if it includes another point A then there would be an Ai with AAi < d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d > 0$ be a fixed positive real number, and let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (for $n = 2$ or $n = 3$) be a bounded body (a compact set with nonempty interior; e.g., a planar region or a solid in space).

(a) (Packing problem.) Determine
\[
P(K,d) \;=\; \max\Bigl\{\,|S| \,:\, S \subseteq K,\ \|x-y\| \ge d \text{ for all distinct } x,y \in S \,\Bigr\},
\]
that is, the largest number of points that can be placed inside $K$ so that every two of the chosen points are at Euclidean distance at least $d$ from one another.

(b) (Covering problem.) Determine
\[
C(K,d) \;=\; \min\Bigl\{\,|T| \,:\, T \subseteq K,\ \forall x \in K\ \exists\, A_i \in T \text{ with } \|x - A_i\| < d \,\Bigr\},
\]
that is, the smallest number of points $\{A_1, A_2, \dots\} \subseteq K$ such that every point $A \in K$ is at distance less than $d$ from at least one $A_i$.

Find closed-form values, exact formulas, or sharp bounds for $P(K,d)$ and $C(K,d)$ for natural classes of bodies $K$ (e.g., disks, squares, regular polygons, balls, cubes), and study their general properties.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical packing/covering by points problem in the plane and in space. Exact values are known only for some special bodies (e.g., small numbers of points in a square, disk, equilateral triangle) and many concrete instances remain open; there is no general formula for arbitrary bodies. The problem in its general form remains open.

status_evidence.title: Packing problems - Erich Friedman
status_evidence.snippet: Collections of best known packings of circles/points in various shapes; many cases are conjectural with no proof of optimality.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal packings/coverings of points in standard bodies remain only partially known.

status_evidence.title: Covering a square by small circles
status_evidence.snippet: Best known coverings; proofs of optimality exist only for small numbers of points.
status_evidence.claim: General covering numbers are not determined.
